Action Plan:
1. Acute left-sided headache: start Ibuprofen 400 mg (oral) every 6–8 h with food as required (max 1.2 g/24 h); may continue Paracetamol; maintain hydration 1.5–2 L water daily and sleep 7–8 h nightly; read supplied “headache red-flag” information and seek urgent review if red-flag symptoms emerge; routine telephone review in 1 week; if no improvement, arrange blood tests and consider alternate diagnoses.
2. Work-related stress/anxiety: self-certify and take up to 1 week off work; self-refer to local counselling service (link provided); continue regular exercise (running ×3/week) and sleep hygiene.
3. Chronic anxiety: continue Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); monitor mood and suicidal ideation; discuss medication review at next follow-up if needed.
4. Safety-netting: low threshold to contact GP sooner if headache worsens, new neurological signs, fever, visual disturbance, vomiting, or other concerns.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: sudden onset severe headache on left side of head, woke patient at 05:30 today; persists at time of call.  
• Character: constant, severe; worse initially on lying down but eases slightly; mild photophobia; no nausea (initial brief dizziness only); no neck stiffness; no fever.  
• Previous headaches: intermittent, milder, frontal “cluster” pattern; never this severe or unilateral.  
• Stressors: high occupational workload for past 2 months, late nights.  
• Past medical history: generalized anxiety disorder ×2 years. No hypertension. No other chronic illnesses or surgeries reported.  
• Medications: Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); single dose Paracetamol taken this morning with minimal relief.  
• Allergies: none known.  
• Social: lives with partner; non-smoker; runs ~3×/week; owns cat; diet “okay”.  
• Family history: mother with anxiety; no family migraines or major physical illnesses.  

Objective:
• Remote consultation; no physical examination performed.  
• No vitals available. No reported fever, neck stiffness, focal neuro deficit, or visual changes.  
• No investigations performed today.  

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute unilateral headache  
   - Assessment: Likely migraine vs tension-type headache.  
   - Differential: cluster headache, secondary causes (e.g., dehydration, stress); low suspicion meningitis/SAH given absence of red-flags.  
   - Investigations planned: none initially; consider blood tests if no improvement at 1-week review.  
   - Treatment planned: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO q6-8h PRN (max 1.2 g/day); may combine with Paracetamol; hydration 1.5–2 L water daily; adequate sleep; patient education on red-flags.  
   - Referrals: none at present.

2. Work-related stress / Anxiety exacerbation  
   - Assessment: Situational stress contributing to headaches; underlying GAD stable.  
   - Investigations planned: none.  
   - Treatment planned: self-certified sick leave up to 7 days; maintain exercise & sleep routine; counselling service self-referral link provided.  
   - Referrals: community counselling/psychological therapy service (self-referral).

3. Chronic anxiety on Sertraline  
   - Assessment: Stable on current regimen; no suicidal ideation.  
   - Treatment planned: continue Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); review effectiveness at next appointment.  
   - Referrals: none now; revisit if symptoms escalate.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: No vitals or physical examination due to tele-consult; unclear Sertraline dose and frequency; no current blood pressure history/values.  
• Internal conflicts: none identified.  
• Transcript quality: clear, minimal background noise; clinically adequate.
